author: lucidota
decision: Explicit supersession of I1..I12 → INV-01..INV-12; schema-1 remains readable (grandfathered); new appends require full fields (schema 2).
evidence: This freeze: 12 supersession records I1..I12 → INV-01..INV-12 in supersessions.jsonl; store.rs SCHEMA=2 with schema-1 read acceptance; tests/hashchain.rs t_schema1_readable.
question: How do prose-only seed records become §56 machine-readable invariants without violating append-only history?
reason: Append-only history is non-negotiable (INV-06); explicit supersession dogfoods the machinery the thesis defends; prose-only rules must never be claimed as enforced (§56).
title: Supersede, don't rewrite: schema-1 seeds stay in the chain (grandfathered readable); INV-01..INV-12 carry the full §56 field set; new appends require full fields (schema 2).

alternatives: Fold unknown arguments into the record
author: lucidota
decision: Unknown k=v arguments are rejected with exit 2 (usage error); unknown fields at the store API level are rejected with exit 4 (semantic error) by the schema-2 allowlist.
evidence: Negative-path probe 2026-10-08: `canon add-principle ... verified=true` → exit 2 with 'unknown argument(s): verified — rejected, never silently dropped'; store-level probe via tests/hashchain.rs t_schema_validation.
question: What happens when a caller passes an argument the canon CLI does not define?
reason: Silent dropping lets a caller believe they set something they did not (false authority); smuggling lets callers invent fields (fake verified flags). Found live during the §56 freeze: verified=true was silently dropped before this fix.
title: Unknown CLI arguments are rejected (exit 2), never silently dropped and never smuggled into records.

decision: Hash-chain correctness is established by tests/hashchain.rs: canonical encoding, prev-hash linkage, corruption detection, mid-file truncation, end-truncation boundary via receipt heads, duplicate detection, concurrent append, malformed-record behavior, schema-2 validation, schema-1 readability, receipt determinism.
evidence: cargo test: 8 unit + hashchain_suite (11 cases) green 2026-10-08; canon audit exit 0.
question: What does 'hash chains proven' mean for the §56 freeze?
reason: Corruption must be detected by the machinery itself, not asserted; the end-truncation boundary must be stated honestly (the chain alone cannot see a cleanly truncated tail).
title: Hash-chain test scope for the §56 freeze
